answer: A trellis of mutual attestation resists Sybil attacks the way a dune field resists a single footprint: each new identity must earn endorsements from established, non-kin peers who stake reputation on it, and endorsements decay unless renewed through real work. A falcon cannot fake a flock — one operator spinning up a thousand sock-puppets gains nothing, because each puppet needs costly sponsorship from peers who lose standing if they vouch for frauds. Identities stay cheap to create, but trusted standing becomes expensive, slow, and traceable, so attack cost scales with influence sought.
